newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain still sees need for Zaire aid force.
newsitem.headline: Spain still sees need for Zaire aid force.

text.p: Spain believes a multinational force should still mount a humanitarian mission to Zaire despite the mass return of refugees to Rwanda but its task should be redefined, a Spanish government official said on Monday.
"The situation is very critical and we still need troops. At least that is our position," said the foreign ministry official, who asked not to be named.
"We have to redefine our mission. I think the reality is forcing all countries to redefine it."
The official told Reuters fewer soldiers may now be needed in the force but added: "We are still preparing for the mission."
Spain, along with France, led calls for international military intervention to open humanitarian corridors so aid could reach more than a million refugees in eastern Zaire.
But the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Monday half a million Hutu refugees had now crossed back into Rwanda from Zaire.
Countries planning to contribute troops to the Canadian-led mission were due to meet in Stuttgart on Wednesday to review the force's size and mandate following the refugees' return.
U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Sunday that Washington had yet to make a firm decision on participation.
France and Canada, backed by the United Nations, said the mission should go ahead.
